item.title: FG coming with major agric reforms to boost food production, cut inflation — ADENLE
item.description: The Federal Government (FG) has proposed sweeping reforms in the agricultural sector, including digitalisation, mechanisation and improved coordination among government agencies in the sector, to boost food production, reduce food inflation and strengthen food security. Senior Special Adviser on Agricultural Innovation to the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, Professor Ademola Adenle, disclosed this in an interview where he outlined plans to resolve long-standing challenges in the sector. Adenle said digitalisation will help government identify genuine farmers, monitor production, ensure transparent distribution of inputs and expand farmers’ access to markets. He said the National Agricultural Growth initiative had introduced a system where agro-dealers distribute inputs to verified farmers while monitoring their output. According to him, the intervention has increased production by 30%, with wheat output rising from 420,000 tonnes to 480,000 tonnes annually. He, however, admitted that higher production alone would not bring down food prices unless institutional weaknesses and structural inefficiencies were addressed. “Previous programmes focused mainly on production and input distribution without addressing institutional capacity, food security and agro-industrialisation,” he said. Adenle called for an overhaul of the ministry’s administrative and legal structures, noting that bureaucratic bottlenecks had limited the impact of interventions. He identified poor coordination among federal, state and local governments as a major challenge, and advocated harmonised agricultural policies across the three tiers. He also proposed performance-based financing, annual key performance indicators, stronger monitoring and evaluation, data-driven decision-making, and legislation to promote accountability and transparency. On rising food prices, Adenle blamed illegal movement of produce across Nigeria’s borders and hoarding of food commodities for creating artificial scarcity. He said the Nigeria Customs Service and the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission are working with security agencies to address the problem. The warning came as the organisations unveiled two reports examining Nigeria’s Energy Transition Plan and the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) of five African countries at a media presentation in Lagos. The reports, titled Four Years On: Examining Nigeria’s Just Transition Plan and Nationally Determined Contributions in Africa: A Five-Country Policy Analysis, assessed the climate commitments of Nigeria, Cameroon, South Africa, Togo and Uganda. They identified fossil fuel expansion, uncertain climate financing, carbon markets and the growing influence of private corporations in climate policy development as major threats to achieving a genuinely just transition across the continent. Speaking, the Executive Director of CAPPA, Akinbode Oluwafemi, said the central question was whether African climate policies were genuinely transforming economies and protecting people or creating fresh opportunities for corporate interests to profit while communities bear the consequences. He said: “These reports emerge from a fundamental concern: Are Africa’s climate policies genuinely transforming our economies and protecting our people, or are they creating new opportunities for corporate interests to profit while communities bear the consequences?” Oluwafemi said governments could not claim to be pursuing decarbonisation while simultaneously approving projects and infrastructure that entrenched dependence on fossil fuels. He cited the contradictions in Uganda, where French multinational TotalEnergies promotes investments in renewable energy, including solar, while remaining a leading developer of the East African Crude Oil Pipeline, EACOP, and the Tilenga oil project. He also referenced Cameroon’s award of five of nine oil blocks offered to fossil fuel operators, including Murphy Oil and Octavia Energy, despite its stated decarbonisation commitments. In Nigeria, the report identified a major contradiction between the country’s ambition to achieve net-zero emissions by 2060 and its official target of producing three million barrels of crude oil daily by 2030. It acknowledged progress in renewable energy deployment and policy development but argued that the country’s energy transition was being layered onto an economy still heavily dependent on oil and gas. The report also questioned the promotion of natural gas as a clean transition fuel, warning that methane, its principal component, is a powerful greenhouse gas responsible, alongside methane emissions from other sources, for nearly 30 per cent of global warming since the Industrial Revolution. According to the organisations, the challenge is not merely setting climate targets but establishing institutions, financing arrangements and enforceable social protections capable of delivering them. They noted that Nigeria’s Energy Transition Plan lacked sufficiently enforceable guarantees for workers and communities affected by the transition, particularly in areas where livelihoods depend on oil and gas activities. The report further highlighted the scale of Nigeria’s energy access challenge, citing World Bank figures showing that more than 80 million Nigerians lacked access to electricity as of March 2025. It argued that a successful transition must deliver affordable and reliable electricity, secure livelihoods, environmental restoration and viable economic alternatives for communities in the Niger Delta and other extraction zones. On climate financing, the reports raised concerns about the growing dependence of African countries on international funding, particularly loans that could deepen their debt burden. Nigeria estimates that it requires $337 billion between 2026 and 2035 to implement its climate commitments, with 80 per cent expected from international funding. Similarly, Togo has made 69.9 per cent of its financing requirements conditional on international support, while South Africa’s NDC indicates that approximately 80 per cent of international financial support recorded for 2021 and 2022 came in the form of loans. item.title: Agbazuere backs Otti’s second-term bid after U-turn
item.description: Dismisses alleged anti-Ngwa remark, cautions critics By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—Former Chief of Staff to ex-Governor Okezie Ikpeazu, Prof. ACB Agbazuere, who was a vocal critic of Governor Alex Otti during the 2019 governorship election, has declared support for the governor’s re-election bid, saying he deserves a second term. Agbazuere, now a member of Otti’s Campaign Advisory Council, also dismissed an allegation attributed to former Commissioner, Chief Charles Ogbonnaya, that the governor allegedly described Ngwa people as brainless, describing the claim as unfounded and politically motivated. Speaking during a radio interview simulcast across several stations in Abia on Tuesday, Agbazuere cautioned politicians against making unsubstantiated allegations, warning that defamatory statements could attract legal consequences under Nigerian laws, including the Cybercrimes Act. He said the allegation would not undermine Otti’s support base, particularly among the Ngwa people. “Dr Alex Otti may love peace; Dr Alex Otti may not want trouble, but they should see that people like us are now with him. Anybody who wants to say anything should be careful and say what he knows to be true,” he warned. Explaining his support for the governor, Agbazuere said the Otti administration had demonstrated commitment to infrastructure development, urban renewal, workers’ welfare and good governance. He cited the reconstruction of Port Harcourt Road and Bank Road in Aba, the Omenuko Bridge and Arochukwu Road as evidence of the administration’s infrastructure drive. He also commended the governor for what he described as regular payment of salaries, pensions and gratuities, as well as improvements in allowances for traditional rulers. On criticisms that increased federal allocations should have translated into more development projects, Agbazuere argued that the rising cost of construction materials must be considered. He cited the increase in the price of cement from about ₦2,000 to ₦12,000 per bag as an example of the inflationary pressures facing construction projects. He challenged critics to visit the state and assess ongoing projects rather than evaluate the administration from a distance. Describing Otti as a banker and trained economist, Agbazuere said the governor understood accountability and prudent management of public resources. He urged Abians to look beyond party affiliations and support continuity, arguing that a second term would enable Otti to complete ongoing projects and consolidate his administration’s programmes. He also recalled that during the 2023 governorship election, a leading opposition candidate had reportedly acknowledged Otti as the best candidate. item.title: How AI is helping Nigerian farmers tackle crop diseases, improve farm decisions
item.description: By Cynthia Alo With many Nigerian farmers still relying on traditional knowledge to identify crop diseases and determine appropriate treatments, delayed access to agricultural advice often means problems are left unresolved until they affect yields. In some cases, farmers have to wait days for agronomists to visit their farms and recommend solutions. CropCura, a digital agricultural innovation co-founded by Victor Onyekachukwu, is seeking to change this practice by bringing crop diagnosis and farm advisory services directly to farmers through technology. Onyekachukwu said the application allows farmers to take pictures of affected crops and receive an AI-powered analysis and recommendations on possible solutions in less than a minute. Apart from crop diagnosis, the platform provides weather information, an AI advisory service and digital farm mapping which allow farmers to access information needed to make decisions about their farms. He said the innovation also addresses another longstanding challenge in Nigerian agriculture which is farmers’ difficulty accessing formal credit because of inadequate records. Through digital farm profiles containing information about farmers, their locations, crops and farm sizes, Onyekachukwu said the technology will also combine a credit-scoring system that can help financial institutions assess farmers for lending. The platform, he said, currently has more than 2,000 farmers, who have mapped over 10,000 hectares of farmland. However, Onyekachukwu identified language barriers, limited smartphone access, low digital literacy and farmers’ distrust of technology as obstacles to wider adoption. He said the government should introduce policies recognising verified digital farm profiles as acceptable evidence for accessing agricultural loans and grants. item.description: By Cynthia Alo Agricultural experts have attributed the disconnect between farmers, researchers and policymakers as a major factor undermining the effectiveness of agricultural policies and interventions. This is even as they called for greater farmer participation in research design and policy formulation. According to them, research priorities were often determined without adequate consideration of farmers’ immediate needs, while policy implementation was constrained by funding limitations, institutional bottlenecks and poor communication of research findings. The experts spoke during the virtual inaugural episode of the Agricultural Policy Circle, organised by Farmosphere, with the theme, “Finding the Gap where Research, Policy, and Practice disconnect.” Agriculture researcher, Ifunanya Orisekeh,said research questions were sometimes determined before researchers reached farming communities, leaving farmers to respond to problems that might not reflect their immediate realities. She said research agendas were often shaped by funding calls, academic requirements and institutional timelines, while the time required to generate findings further widened the gap between research and practice. She said: “Research agendas are shaped before a funding call comes up. For example, if there is a project that needs a student already set, by the time you reach the field, the question is already printed and the farmer is there to answer your question. “So we can become very good in the research perspective. item.title: COCEFAAA appoints new directors to strengthen cocoa, coffee farmers’ interests
item.description: By Kafayat Kokumo The Cocoa and Coffee Farmers Alliance Association of Africa (COCEFAAA) has appointed some stakeholders to its Board of Directors and country leadership positions to strengthen the representation and protection of cocoa and coffee farmers across West, East and Central Africa. item.title: SMEs: NADF, Sahel Capital sign MoU to reduce borrowing costs
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA – IN a bid to boost agribusiness, the National Agricultural Development Fund, NADF and Sahel Capital Fund Manager Limited have signed a Memorandum of Understanding, MoU, to expand access to affordable financing for Small and Medium Enterprises, SMEs, in the agricultural sector. The partnership which seeks to unlock more private-sector investments in agriculture, is expected to reduce the cost of borrowing for agribusinesses through innovative blended financing arrangements. Speaking at the signing ceremony, Executive Secretary, NADF, Muhammed Ibrahim, said the agreement marked a deliberate shift from conventional agricultural financing towards building an investment ecosystem capable of attracting sustainable capital into the sector. Ibrahim explained that NADF would bring its catalytic and development mandates, as well as its understanding of national agricultural priorities, to the partnership, while Sahel Capital would contribute investment expertise, market intelligence and experience across different agricultural value chains. According to him, the collaboration is designed to combine public-sector and concessionary capital with private investment expertise to unlock additional financing opportunities for viable agribusinesses. Under the MoU, both institutions will explore the feasibility of blended financing arrangements through which NADF provide funding alongside capital managed by Sahel Capital, including the Sahel Agribusiness Private Debt Fund, SAPDF. The proposed financing framework may feature risk-sharing mechanisms, concessional financing and other innovative funding structures aimed at improving access to capital for eligible agribusinesses. Sahel Capital is also expected to provide investment structuring, fund management and technical expertise, identify eligible agribusinesses and develop monitoring and reporting frameworks for the proposed facility. Other areas of collaboration include information sharing, development of a pipeline of bankable agribusiness projects, technical assistance and capacity building. Also speaking, Managing Partner, Sahel Capital, Mezuo Nwuneli, explained the partnership basically would help reduce borrowing costs for agribusiness SMEs by combining NADF funding with capital managed by the investment firm. However, Nwuneli lamented many agribusinesses currently obtain loans at interest rates ranging between 24 and 27 per cent, a situation he said makes business expansion, investment in productive capacity and long-term growth difficult. He said that the proposed collaboration would enable both institutions to provide financing at a lower blended cost, improving the financial viability of businesses and freeing up resources for expansion. item.title: LASWA, Interferry complete ferry safety inspection training
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Waterways Authority (LASWA), in partnership with global trade association Interferry, has concluded Module 6 of the Africa Ferry Safety Development and Mentoring Programme to strengthen safety standards across the waterways sector. The training equipped maritime professionals with technical skills to audit and inspect commercial passenger ferries as part of efforts to improve passenger safety and compliance with international maritime standards. The module, titled “Survey and Inspection”, combined self-paced theoretical lessons from the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) and Lloyd’s Register with virtual mentorship and practical field exercises. As part of the programme, participants attended a virtual “Ask the Expert” session on October 21 with Interferry specialists, Joep Bollerman, Francesco Ruisi and Darren Johnston, to discuss international ferry safety standards. This was followed by live condition and safety compliance audits at operational passenger ferry terminals, supervised by Sandra (Okoli) Ubong of ABS and Engr. Frank Fayinto of Lloyd’s Register. During the field exercises, participants applied an eight-step survey methodology covering preparation, onboard assessment and reporting. They were trained to identify safety deficiencies relating to hull integrity, life-saving appliances, fire protection systems and machinery, while applying the 5W+1H principle to ensure evidence-based reporting. The participants also learnt to classify identified risks into immediate, medium-term and low-priority interventions to facilitate timely corrective action. The initiative is supported by the Lagos State Government and the Special Adviser to the Governor on Blue Economy, Mr Oluwadamilola Emmanuel, alongside Interferry Chief Executive Officer, Mike Corrigan, and Ferrysafe Executive Sponsor, Shari Corrigan. With the successful completion of Module 6, the programme is expected to progress to Module 7, titled “Watchkeeping”, scheduled for November 2026. The next phase will further equip participating maritime professionals with competencies in vessel operations, navigational safety and effective watchkeeping practices. LASWA reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening professional standards, improving passenger safety and developing a more efficient, resilient and sustainable water transportation system in Lagos State and across Africa through international collaboration. item.title: Mining: Zamfara task force moves to reclaim gold fields
item.description: The Zamfara State Government inaugurated a 13-man committee to curb illegal mining activities across the state. The Secretary to the Zamfara State Government, Abubakar Mohammad Nakwada, inaugurated the committee on Friday in Gusau, the state capital. This was contained in a statement signed by Mr Sulaiman Tudu, the Senior Special Assistant on Media, Office of the Secretary to the State Government, issued in Gusau on Saturday. The committee, headed by the State’s Commissioner for Environment, Abdulrahman Tumbido, has broad membership across security agencies, traditional institutions, and relevant federal and state government agencies. Inaugurating the committee, Mr Nakwada said the initiative was part of the state government’s efforts to assist the Federal Government in formalising the mining sector in the state. The SSG charged the committee to work closely with security agencies and relevant regulatory and local authorities to identify locations where illegal mining is taking place and profile the operators. The committee will also ensure that even licensed companies comply with relevant laws and regulations, take adequate measures to prevent environmental degradation, and safeguard the safety and rights of host communities. In his remarks, the Chairman of the Committee, Tumbido, said the committee will work with reliable information, respect for the law, fairness and regard for the rights and livelihoods of the people. He added that the committee will ensure that its efforts contribute to lasting security, environmental protection and sustainable development in the state. item.title: Emir Sanusi to Governor Lawal: I am impressed
item.description: The Emir of Kano, Khalifah Muhammadu Sanusi II, has expressed satisfaction with Governor Dauda Lawal’s performance in Zamfara State. The emir was the guest of honour at the commissioning of the rebuilt and equipped Zawiyya Mosque and Islamiyya School in Gusau on Friday. The Zawiyya is one of the oldest Islamic institutions in Zamfara, with a long history of producing scholars across various fields. At the commissioning ceremony, the Emir of Kano, Khalifah Muhammadu Sanusi II, said that only those familiar with the Zawiyya’s former structure could fully appreciate the scale and quality of Governor Lawal’s work. item.title: Sit-at-home: Business activities yet to pick up — Traders
item.description: …An empty street on a sit-at-home day By Steve Oko & Chinedu Adonu Commercial activities are gradually returning to the South-East region after years of an illegal Monday sit-at-home order declared by non-state actors crippled business and social life. While commercial operations are picking up in some states, others continue to lag behind. For example, the Anambra State Government had to forcefully shut down markets in Onitsha and other areas to compel traders to reopen on Mondays, yet many businesses still remained closed. The exact reason for this hesitation remains unclear, as the threat of the sit-at-home order has significantly receded across the region, with the violent attacks and harassment of the past now seldom witnessed. However, findings indicate that many South-East residents have simply grown accustomed to this forced Monday routine after experiencing it for so long. Consequently, many individuals—particularly independent business owners—now voluntarily choose to rest on Mondays. Furthermore, several rural communities have permanently adopted Mondays for communal meetings, neighbourhood policing, road repairs, and other civic activities. Ultimately, what began as a forced restriction has largely transitioned into a voluntary day of rest, effectively extending the weekend by an extra day.In Aba, Abia State, following disruptions associated with the Monday sit-at-home, major markets in the commercial city are yet to fully recover their usual Monday patronage. Aguguo attributed the situation partly to lingering resentment over the continued incarceration of the leader of the Indigenous People of Biafra, IPOB, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, saying some traders and customers were observing the Monday restriction voluntarily as personal expression of solidarity. According to him, the situation is no longer principally about coercion or enforcement by any group, but about what he described as a lingering “wound” in the hearts of some Igbo people over Kanu’s detention. “Aba is gradually recovering, even though customers are not yet coming, especially in the major markets where we deal largely in wholesale. “The issue of sit-at-home is not really about force by IPOB or anybody anymore. He cited Ekeoha Shopping Plaza as an example, saying many traders now open their shops but struggle to attract customers. “In Ekeoha, for instance, people open, but customers are not coming to patronize them. Nobody is forcing anybody, and it is not a government directive. It is simply an individual decision,” he said. A trader is self-employed. The shop is yours and the business is yours, and you can decide when to go out and when not to go out. “What government can do is orientation — make traders understand the implications of losing that extra business day and how it affects their income and families. item.title: Kebbi APC reconciles aggrieved members ahead of 2027 polls
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kebbi State has declared that it is united and strong ahead of the 2027 general elections, following a reconciliation exercise aimed at addressing grievances among party members. The Secretary of the Contact and Reconciliation Committee set up by Governor Nasir Idris, Engineer Ahmed Umar Faruk, made this known on Tuesday in Birnin Kebbi while briefing journalists on the committee’s activities. Faruk said the committee had completed 10 days of engagements across the state’s 21 local government areas, during which it met with aggrieved party members and resolved several complaints. He said those engaged included former commissioners, former members of the state House of Assembly and National Assembly, as well as other party members who felt sidelined or had grievances arising from the concluded party primaries. According to him, the committee recorded significant progress by providing a platform for aggrieved members to express their concerns and ensuring that their complaints received attention. He said the exercise had helped restore unity within the party, adding that the APC leadership in the state was committed to carrying every member along in its activities. “We toured the 21 local government areas in Kebbi State and saw loyalty to the governor and the party from top to bottom,” he said. Faruk urged party leaders at the state, local government and ward levels to sustain regular engagement with members to prevent grievances from accumulating and threatening party unity. He, however, warned members against engaging in anti-party activities and clandestine meetings capable of creating divisions within the APC. He said the party would not tolerate actions capable of undermining its unity as it prepares for the 2027 general elections. item.title: Tinubu Won 2023 Election On His Own, Buhari Didn’t Fully Support Him – APC’s Hassan
item.description: A spokesperson for the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Alwan Hassan, has said President Bola Tinubu won the 2023 presidential election against all odds, insisting that former President Muhammadu Buhari did not fully support his candidacy. Hassan said Tinubu secured victory largely through his own political strength, arguing that Buhari did not actively stand behind the APC candidate during the build-up to the election. He made the remarks on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , while discussing the president’s chances of securing re-election in 2027. During the interview, Hassan was asked whether Tinubu would benefit from the organic political structure and support base associated with his predecessor, particularly as the APC prepares for another presidential contest in the next two months. In response, the APC stalwart questioned whether Buhari had given Tinubu the full backing of his political structure in 2023. “Did he enjoy that in 2023? Did we enjoy Buhari’s support in 2023? Let the truth be told, we did not,” he said. ﻿ When asked whether he was suggesting that Tinubu won the 2023 election on his own, Hassan answered in the affirmative, maintaining that the former president did not fully support his successor’s ambition. “On his own. Buhari didn’t fully come out to support Tinubu,” he said. He further argued that Buhari did not actively campaign for Tinubu during the 2023 election, despite both politicians belonging to the same political party. “Buhari didn’t do well in 2023. He didn’t actually come out to stand for us and stand for Asiwaju in 2023. Asiwaju won that election against all odds,” Hassan said. item.title: [VIDEO] Wike’s ₦10m Pledge: INEC, Police Can Trigger Investigation, Says Okoye
item.description: A former National Commissioner of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Festus Okoye, says the commission, the police and other law enforcement agencies can initiate an investigation into the ₦10 million pledge by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, to councillors ahead of the 2027 general elections. Okoye, a lawyer, said this on Tuesday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today. He said the absence of action by INEC would not prevent individuals or other relevant authorities from raising concerns or investigating the matter if an electoral offence was suspected. “If INEC is not taking this up, can anyone petition on this matter to say, I think Minister Wike is doing the wrong thing? Is it possible? Oh, definitely, yes,” he said. ﻿ The ex-commissioner added that the state could also initiate action if an offence had been committed, while law enforcement agencies could investigate where they believed there were grounds to suspect a violation. Mr Okoye said INEC could equally petition the relevant authorities to investigate the matter and prosecute anyone found culpable. Wike had pledged ₦10 million to each FCT councillor who successfully delivers their ward for President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 elections. item.title: Obi counters Tinubu, defends Anambra erosion record
item.description: Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), has disputed President Bola Tinubu’s criticism of his record on erosion control in Anambra State, insisting that he helped develop the programme currently being used to tackle the environmental challenge. Tinubu had criticised Obi’s tenure as Anambra governor during an All Progressives Congress (APC) rally in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, over the weekend, alleging that the former governor “ran away from erosion” while highlighting environmental projects undertaken in Lagos. However, speaking on Tuesday during an interview on Rhythm FM Jos ahead of the NDC town hall meeting in Plateau State, Obi dismissed the allegation as untrue. The former Anambra governor said he worked with a former Minister of Environment to develop the erosion-control programme, which he said was subsequently adopted following his intervention with the late President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua. “On what the president said while campaigning in Akwa Ibom, it’s not true. I, working with the former minister of environment, developed what they’re using today to fight erosion,” Obi said. “I went to President Yar’Adua, made a suggestion to him. He called the minister and said he should go and develop it.” Obi governed Anambra State from 2006 to 2014, during which the state faced significant erosion challenges. At the Uyo rally, Tinubu had questioned Obi’s preparedness for the presidency, citing the erosion problem in Anambra as an example of what he described as shortcomings in his record as governor. Explaining his visit to Plateau State, Obi said it was part of his approach to engaging citizens and understanding their challenges before embarking on campaign rallies. He argued that political candidates should first listen to the concerns and experiences of the people before explaining how they intend to address them. The NDC candidate also identified insecurity in central Nigeria as a major challenge, stressing the need to ensure that residents could return to their communities, pursue their businesses and engage in farming without fear. He said his administration, if elected, would prioritise public services, particularly education and healthcare, as well as insurance coverage for vulnerable Nigerians. “Unless children go to school without fear, unless parents go to farms without fear, we don’t have a country,” he said. “You cannot stay in a developing country and a developing world if you have poor health accessibility and poor education accessibility. Education and health are the foundation for development. I will invest in them.” The post Obi counters Tinubu, defends Anambra erosion record appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NDC Alleges Plot To Disrupt Obi’s Benue Visit, Govt Denies Claim
item.description: The Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused the Benue State Government of plotting to disrupt the planned visit of its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to the state, an allegation the government has dismissed as false. Obi is scheduled to visit Benue State on Wednesday for a town hall meeting in Makurdi and a humanitarian visit to Yelewata, where he is expected to pay tribute to victims of the June 2025 massacre and commiserate with their families. Addressing journalists in Makurdi on Tuesday, the party’s governorship candidate in the state, Terhemba Shija, called on the state government and security agencies to guarantee the safety of Obi and his supporters. Shija alleged that the government had issued threats aimed at preventing the former Anambra State governor from visiting Yelewata, recalling an earlier attempt to stop him from visiting the community. For businesses, content creators, and people researching social media trends, another question can be just as interesting: which accounts does that person choose to follow? Someone may publicly promote fashion, technology, or entertainment while following creators in entirely different fields. A business account may begin following emerging influencers long before announcing a collaboration. A public figure may gradually change the types of accounts appearing on their Following list. These observations can provide useful context, particularly when viewed over time. An Instagram following tracker helps organize changes to the accounts a public Instagram profile follows. Rather than relying on a single snapshot, tools such as Snoopreport record detected follows and unfollows across reporting periods. The results can support social media research, although they cannot explain why someone followed an account or reveal information that Instagram keeps private. Instagram allows users to inspect the Following list of an accessible public profile. However, the list doesn’t provide a dependable chronological history of when each connection was added. The order in which accounts appear should not be treated as a reliable record of recent follows. To understand changes, the list needs to be observed across different periods. What Changes in the Following List Can Tell You Imagine a small fashion retailer researching potential brand ambassadors. A popular stylist’s profile looks promising, but the retailer wants to understand which types of creators, labels, and businesses attract the stylist’s attention. A single visit to the Following list offers a snapshot. Regular observations can reveal which accounts were added or removed during a particular period. If the stylist begins following several sustainable clothing labels, the retailer might investigate whether environmentally conscious fashion is becoming a more prominent topic in that creator’s public activity. The important word is might . Following an account is not an endorsement, a commercial agreement, or confirmation of an individual’s private interests. The value comes from generating research questions that can be checked against public posts, published partnerships, and other evidence. How Snoopreport Tracks Public Following Activity Snoopreport is a service that monitors certain publicly observable Instagram actions and organizes detected changes into reports. Its Instagram following tracker focuses on accounts that a selected public profile begins or stops following. The process starts with an Instagram username. Users don’t need to provide their own Instagram password. Once an eligible public account is added, Snoopreport begins collecting detectable activity and presents the findings in weekly and monthly reports. These reports can help users identify: Accounts the tracked profile recently followed. Accounts it stopped following during a reporting period. Changes that appear across successive weeks or months. A regular report establishes that a detected change occurred within a period. It doesn’t provide a guaranteed exact timestamp or explain the reason behind the action. The service does not provide access to private profiles, direct messages, or information about who viewed someone’s Stories. An account may add several new connections in one week and remove others the following month. Without a record, those changes may be difficult to reconstruct later. An Instagram following tracker makes comparisons easier by grouping detected activity into defined reporting periods. Weekly reports can be useful when examining a developing topic, such as the emergence of a new group of creators in a particular industry. Monthly reports offer a broader perspective, helping separate recurring interests from isolated additions. For example, if a public business profile repeatedly follows entrepreneurs working in renewable energy, that pattern may be worth exploring. But the observation should be interpreted carefully. It could reflect market research, general curiosity, networking, or another explanation entirely. A pattern is a reason to investigate, not a conclusion. In its official explanation of Following and Favorites , Meta describes a chronological Following feed that displays posts from accounts a user follows. It doesn’t tell an observer which accounts another person followed last week. This distinction matters because social media platforms offer several features with similar names but very different capabilities. A company may observe public profiles within its industry and use changes in their connections as clues for finding unfamiliar creators, businesses, or communities. Journalists and media researchers may also find the information useful when studying publicly visible networks around a cultural trend. The data can also complement conventional social media research. Rather than treating a follow as evidence of a relationship, analysts can compare it with published content, public announcements, and direct statements. This approach is especially important where a mistaken conclusion could affect someone’s reputation.
